A torn/garbage tail\n62\t    line — a partial write from a crash — is SKIPPED so a read/restart never blows up on it: we return\n63\t    the last line that JSON-parses and carries the chain fields (FIX 2). None if no valid line exists.\n64\t    For a clean file this returns exactly the last non-empty line, byte-for-byte as before.\"\"\"\n65\t    try:\n66\t        size = path.stat().st_size\n67\t    except OSError:\n68\t        return None\n69\t    if size == 0:\n70\t        return None\n71\t    window = 8192\n72\t    while True:\n73\t        start = max(0, size - window)\n74\t        with path.open(\"rb\") as f:\n75\t            f.seek(start)\n76\t            buf = f.read(size - start)\n77\t        lines = [ln for ln in buf.split(b\"\\n\") if ln.strip()]\n78\t        if start > 0 and lines:\n79\t            lines = lines[1:]                       # the first line may be partial unless we are at BOF\n80\t        for raw in reversed(lines):\n81\t            try:\n82\t                d = json.loads(raw)\n83\t            except ValueError:\n84\t                d = None\n85\t            if isinstance(d, dict) and all(k in d for k in _REQUIRED_KEYS):\n86\t                return raw.decode(\"utf-8\")\n87\t            _log.warning(\"spine: skipping malformed tail line while seeking the tip (%s)\", path)\n88\t        if start == 0:\n89\t            return None                             # scanned the whole file, no valid line\n90\t        window *= 4                                 # a torn tail bigger than the window (rare) — widen\n91\t\n92\t\n93\tdef _last_valid_boundary(path: Path) -> \"tuple[int, ChainEntry | None]\":\n94\t    \"\"\"Return (byte offset just past the last VALID record line, its ChainEntry) — bytes BEYOND that\n95\t    offset are a torn tail from an interrupted write, which `append` truncates before writing so the new\n96\t    record cannot merge with them and be silently lost (BLOCK-1). (0, None) for an empty / all-torn file.\n97\t    For a clean file the offset equals the file size (nothing to truncate).\"\"\"\n98\t    try:\n99\t        size = path.stat().st_size\n100\t    except OSError:\n101\t        return 0, None\n102\t    if size == 0:\n103\t        return 0, None\n104\t    window = 8192\n105\t    while True:\n106\t        start = max(0, size - window)\n107\t        with path.open(\"rb\") as f:\n108\t            f.seek(start)\n109\t            buf = f.read(size - start)\n110\t        segs: list[tuple[int, bytes]] = []          # (byte offset just past this line's \\n, line bytes)\n111\t        i = 0\n112\t        while True:\n113\t            nl = buf.find(b\"\\n\", i)\n114\t            if nl == -1:\n115\t                break\n116\t            segs.append((start + nl + 1, buf[i:nl]))\n117\t            i = nl + 1\n118\t        for end, raw in reversed(segs):             # near-EOF first; front partials (start>0) never win\n119\t            if not raw.strip():\n120\t                continue\n121\t            try:\n122\t                d = json.loads(raw)\n123\t            except ValueError:\n124\t                d = None\n125\t            if isinstance(d, dict) and all(k in d for k in _REQUIRED_KEYS):\n126\t                return end, ChainEntry(seq=d[\"seq\"], prev_hash=d[\"prev_hash\"],\n127\t                                       cert_digest=d[\"cert_digest\"], entry_hash=d[\"entry_hash\"])\n128\t            _log.warning(\"spine: skipping malformed tail segment while seeking the tip (%s)\", path)\n129\t        if start == 0:\n130\t            return 0, None\n131\t        window *= 4\n132\t\n133\t\n134\tclass SpineStore:\n135\t    def __init__(self, path: Path | str = SPINE_PATH) -> None:\n136\t        # `self.path` is the STABLE identity + lock token (…/spine.jsonl). After a migration it is renamed\n137\t        # away and no longer a data file, but it remains the key for the in-process RLock and the anchor\n138\t        # the whole layout derives from — so the RLock that `envelope.consume` shares with `append` stays\n139\t        # the same object across a rotation (invariant 14). All DATA I/O targets `self._active` (the\n140\t        # manifest's active segment, or — with no manifest yet — the legacy single file in place, which is\n141\t        # byte-identical to the pre-rotation store).\n142\t        self.path = Path(path)\n143\t        self.path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n144\t        self._layout = SpineLayout.for_path(self.path)\n145\t        # NB: `segments/` is created only when actually migrating/rotating (not on every construction), so a\n146\t        # legacy/fresh store leaves the spine dir byte-identical to today (no stray empty dirs).\n147\t        self._manifest: Manifest | None = read_manifest(self._layout)\n148\t        self._reconcile_orphan_migration()          # complete a migrate() interrupted before the manifest write\n149\t        self._active: Path = self._resolve_active_path()\n150\t        # seq -> byte-offset index (FIX 1). Built lazily on the first TARGETED read (get / iter_records\n151\t        # with since_seq >= 0) and then kept current: maintained O(1) on our own appends, and extended\n152\t        # (never rewritten — an append-only file's offsets never move) when a stat shows another PROCESS\n153\t        # grew the file. Full scans (verify/count/entries/iter_records(-1)) never touch it, staying a\n154\t        # single byte-identical pass. `_index_lock` guards the dict against concurrent read+append.\n155\t        # Slice 0/1: the index is single-segment (over `self._active`); it is (segment, offset)-aware in\n156\t        # a later slice. It is invalidated whenever the active segment changes under us.\n157\t        self._index_lock = threading.Lock()\n158\t        self._index_built = False\n159\t        self._offsets: dict[int, int] = {}\n160\t        self._max_seq = -1\n161\t        self._scan_pos = 0                          # byte offset just past the last COMPLETE line indexed\n162\t        self._last: ChainEntry | None = self._read_last_entry()\n163\t\n164\t    # --- segment layout / manifest ------------------------------------------------\n165\t    def _resolve_active_path(self) -> Path:\n166\t        \"\"\"The current append/read target. With a manifest, the active segment's absolute path; without\n167\t        one (a fresh or not-yet-migrated legacy spine), the legacy single file in place — byte-identical\n168\t        to the pre-rotation store, so nothing destructive happens until an explicit `migrate()`.\"\"\"\n169\t        if self._manifest is not None:\n170\t            act = self._manifest.active()\n171\t            if act is not None:\n172\t                return self._layout.seg_path(act)\n173\t        return self.path\n174\t\n175\t    @contextmanager\n176\t    def _crossproc_lock(self) -> \"Iterator[None]\":\n177\t        \"\"\"Cross-process exclusion on the inode-stable lockfile (invariant 14 / D3). flock binds to the\n178\t        open file DESCRIPTION, not the path, so an os.replace of the manifest/segments cannot move the\n179\t        lock out from under a concurrent writer — which the prior flock-on-the-data-fd could not survive.\n180\t        Best-effort exactly as before (fcntl absent on non-POSIX; a flock failure is swallowed).\"\"\"\n181\t        if fcntl is None:  # pragma: no cover — non-POSIX\n182\t            yield\n183\t            return\n184\t        self._layout.lockfile_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n185\t        fd = os.open(str(self._layout.lockfile_path), os.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT, 0o600)\n186\t        try:\n187\t            try:\n188\t                fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX)\n189\t            except OSError:  # pragma: no cover\n190\t                pass\n191\t            yield\n192\t        finally:\n193\t            os.close(fd)\n194\t\n195\t    def _refresh_active_under_lock(self) -> None:\n196\t        \"\"\"MUST hold `_crossproc_lock`. Re-resolve the active segment from the manifest so an appender\n197\t        constructed BEFORE a concurrent migrate()/rotation writes to the CURRENT active target, never a\n198\t        stale path — which would fork the log or resurrect a renamed-away file (the split-brain the\n199\t        two-step migration guards against). Cheap: the manifest is tiny (Slice 1 gates this on a change\n200\t        token).\"\"\"\n201\t        m = read_manifest(self._layout)\n202\t        new_active = self.path\n203\t        act = m.active() if m is not None else None\n204\t        if act is not None:\n205\t            new_active = self._layout.seg_path(act)\n206\t        if new_active != self._active or (m is not None) != (self._manifest is not None):\n207\t            self._manifest = m\n208\t            self._active = new_active\n209\t            self._invalidate_index()\n210\t            self._last = self._read_last_entry()\n211\t\n212\t    def _invalidate_index(self) -> None:\n213\t        \"\"\"MUST hold `_index_lock` OR be on a path with no concurrent index use. Drops the single-segment\n214\t        index so the next read rebuilds it against the (possibly changed) active segment.\"\"\"\n215\t        with self._index_lock:\n216\t            self._index_built = False\n217\t            self._offsets = {}\n218\t            self._max_seq = -1\n219\t            self._scan_pos = 0\n220\t\n221\t    def _reconcile_orphan_migration(self) -> None:\n222\t        \"\"\"Close the migrate() crash window. migrate() does an ATOMIC `os.replace(spine.jsonl →\n223\t        segments/seg-00000000.jsonl)` and THEN publishes the manifest; a crash BETWEEN them leaves seg-0\n224\t        present, `spine.jsonl` gone, and no manifest — at which point the legacy fallback (active =\n225\t        spine.jsonl) would read the spine as EMPTY and silently hide all history. The rename is atomic and\n226\t        already durable, so if we observe exactly that state we simply finish the interrupted migration by\n227\t        publishing the manifest (idempotent, under the cross-process lock). (os.replace is atomic, so\n228\t        spine.jsonl and seg-0 are never both present or both absent from a torn rename — this one state is\n229\t        the whole window.)\"\"\"\n230\t        if self._manifest is not None:\n231\t            return\n232\t        seg0 = self._layout.segments_dir / segment_filename(0)\n233\t        if not (seg0.exists() and not self.path.exists()):\n234\t            return\n235\t        with self._crossproc_lock():\n236\t            if read_manifest(self._layout) is None and seg0.exists() and not self.path.exists():\n237\t                write_manifest(self._layout,\n238\t                               initial_manifest(SCOPE, active_file=f\"segments/{segment_filename(0)}\"))\n239\t                _log.warning(\"spine: completed an interrupted migration — published the manifest for %s\", seg0)\n240\t            self._manifest = read_manifest(self._layout)\n241\t\n242\t    def migrate(self) -> bool:\n243\t        \"\"\"Move a legacy single-file spine into the segment layout: rename `spine.jsonl` →\n244\t        `segments/seg-00000000.jsonl` (atomic, same filesystem — O(1), no byte copy) and publish a\n245\t        single-active-segment manifest. Idempotent (a no-op once a manifest exists). Returns True iff it\n246\t        migrated. SPLIT-BRAIN SAFETY: run this only after every spine writer is on code that flocks the\n247\t        path-stable lockfile (this Slice-0 code) and re-resolves the active segment under that lock — so\n248\t        no old-style appender writes to `spine.jsonl` through the former data-fd flock while this runs.\n249\t        After migration `spine.jsonl` is absent and is NEVER re-created as a data file (all data I/O\n250\t        targets the active segment).\"\"\"\n251\t        with spine_lock(self.path):\n252\t            with self._crossproc_lock():\n253\t                if read_manifest(self._layout) is not None:\n254\t                    self._refresh_active_under_lock()\n255\t                    return False\n256\t                self._layout.segments_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n257\t                seg0_rel = f\"segments/{segment_filename(0)}\"\n258\t                seg0_abs = self._layout.segments_dir / segment_filename(0)\n259\t                if self.path.exists():\n260\t                    os.replace(self.path, seg0_abs)         # atomic rename (same fs); O(1), no copy\n261\t                else:\n262\t                    seg0_abs.touch()                        # fresh spine: create the empty active segment\n263\t                fsync_dir(self._layout.segments_dir)\n264\t                write_manifest(self._layout, initial_manifest(SCOPE, active_file=seg0_rel))\n265\t                self._manifest = read_manifest(self._layout)\n266\t                self._active = self._resolve_active_path()\n267\t                self._invalidate_index()\n268\t                self._last = self._read_last_entry()\n269\t                return True\n270\t\n271\t    # --- write --------------------------------------------------------------------\n272\t    def append(\n273\t        self, *, kind: str, source: str, actor: str, payload: dict[str, Any],\n274\t        parent_id: int | None = None, supersedes_id: int | None = None,\n275\t        ts: str | None = None,\n276\t    ) -> int:\n277\t        content = {\n278\t            \"scope\": SCOPE, \"kind\": kind, \"source\": source, \"actor\": actor,\n279\t            \"payload\": payload, \"parent_id\": parent_id, \"supersedes_id\": supersedes_id,\n280\t        }\n281\t        cert_digest = digest_payload(content)  # wallclock-free\n282\t        # Serialize the whole read-tip → write so concurrent writers (threaded bridge server, gesture\n283\t        # daemon) can't both fork off a stale tip and break the chain. The in-process RLock is keyed on\n284\t        # the STABLE `self.path` (unchanged), so the check-then-append gate `envelope.consume` builds on\n285\t        # top of it stays atomic across a rotation. Re-read the TRUE tip from disk under the lock.\n286\t        with spine_lock(self.path):\n287\t            with self._crossproc_lock():                 # cross-process guard on the path-stable lockfile\n288\t                self._refresh_active_under_lock()        # pick up a concurrent migrate()/rotation; never fork\n289\t                active = self._active\n290\t                # binary append+read: lets us TRUNCATE a torn tail before writing (BLOCK-1 fix). `a+b`\n291\t                # creates the file if absent and — in append mode — every write still lands at EOF.\n292\t                with active.open(\"a+b\") as f:\n293\t                    # BLOCK-1: an interrupted write can leave torn bytes PAST the last valid record. Appending\n294\t                    # after them would MERGE (torn + new) into one unparseable line → the new record is silently\n295\t                    # lost, verify() stays green, and a lost kill-switch panic never halts the mesh. Truncate the\n296\t                    # dead tail back to the last valid record FIRST (this only removes never-committed garbage\n297\t                    # from an interrupted write; committed records are untouched). Evaluated on the ACTIVE\n298\t                    # segment under the lock (invariant 7 — the append target is always the true chain tip).\n299\t                    clean_end, last = _last_valid_boundary(active)\n300\t                    pre_size = os.fstat(f.fileno()).st_size\n301\t                    if pre_size > clean_end:\n302\t                        f.truncate(clean_end)\n303\t                        _log.warning(\"spine: truncated a %d-byte torn tail (interrupted write) before append (%s)\",\n304\t                                     pre_size - clean_end, active)\n305\t                    entry = append_entry([last], cert_digest) if last else build_chain([cert_digest])[0]\n306\t                    record = {\n307\t                        \"seq\": entry.seq, **content, \"ts\": ts or now_iso(),\n308\t                        \"cert_digest\": cert_digest, \"prev_hash\": entry.prev_hash, \"entry_hash\": entry.entry_hash,\n309\t                    }\n310\t                    line = json.dumps(record, ensure_ascii=False) + \"\\n\"\n311\t                    offset = clean_end                      # after any truncate, EOF == clean_end (where the line lands)\n312\t                    f.write(line.encode(\"utf-8\"))\n313\t                    f.flush()\n314\t                    os.fsync(f.fileno())                    # FIX 3: an ack'd append is durable across a crash\n315\t                    # FIX 1: keep the index current with NO re-scan when it is already exactly up to date.\n316\t                    # If another PROCESS appended in between, `_scan_pos < offset` and we skip here — the next\n317\t                    # read's `_ensure_index` extends from `_scan_pos`, picking up the gap records AND this one.\n318\t                    with self._index_lock:\n319\t                        if self._index_built and self._scan_pos == offset:\n320\t                            self._offsets[entry.seq] = offset\n321\t                            if entry.seq > self._max_seq:\n322\t                                self._max_seq = entry.seq\n323\t                            self._scan_pos = offset + len(line.encode(\"utf-8\"))\n324\t                self._last = entry\n325\t        return entry.seq\n326\t\n327\t    # --- read ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n328\t    def iter_records(self, *, since_seq: int = -1) -> Iterator[SpineRecord]:\n329\t        \"\"\"Records with seq > `since_seq`, in order. FIX 1: for since_seq >= 0 the index seeks straight\n330\t        to the first wanted line (O(records-returned), not O(file)); a full read (since_seq < 0) starts\n331\t        at byte 0 exactly as before. FIX 2: a line that fails to parse or lacks required keys is SKIPPED\n332\t        (a torn tail no longer crashes the read); a torn MIDDLE line becomes a seq gap that verify() fails\n333\t        on, so mid-file tampering is never silently hidden.\"\"\"\n334\t        if not self._active.exists():\n335\t            return\n336\t        start_off = self._start_offset_for(since_seq)\n337\t        with self._active.open(\"rb\") as f:\n338\t            if start_off:\n339\t                f.seek(start_off)\n340\t            for raw in f:\n341\t                if not raw.strip():\n342\t                    continue\n343\t                try:\n344\t                    rec = SpineRecord.from_dict(json.loads(raw))\n345\t                except (ValueError, KeyError, TypeError):\n346\t                    _log.warning(\"spine: skipping malformed line during iter_records (%s)\", self._active)\n347\t                    continue\n348\t                if rec.seq > since_seq:\n349\t                    yield rec\n350\t\n351\t    def get(self, seq: int) -> SpineRecord | None:\n352\t        \"\"\"A single record by seq — O(1) via the index (FIX 1), byte-identical to a full scan.\"\"\"\n353\t        if seq < 0 or not self._active.exists():\n354\t            return None\n355\t        self._ensure_index()\n356\t        with self._index_lock:\n357\t            off = self._offsets.get(seq)\n358\t        if off is not None:\n359\t            with self._active.open(\"rb\") as f:\n360\t                f.seek(off)\n361\t                raw = f.readline()\n362\t            try:\n363\t                rec = SpineRecord.from_dict(json.loads(raw))\n364\t            except (ValueError, KeyError, TypeError):\n365\t                return None\n366\t            return rec if rec.seq == seq else None\n367\t        # not indexed (beyond the tip, or a corrupt line was skipped) — bounded fallback (still index-seeked)\n368\t        for r in self.iter_records(since_seq=seq - 1):\n369\t            if r.seq == seq:\n370\t                return r\n371\t            if r.seq > seq:\n372\t                break\n373\t        return None\n374\t\n375\t    def tail(self, n: int) -> list[SpineRecord]:\n376\t        \"\"\"The last `n` records, seek-from-end (O(n) bytes, NOT O(file)) — for a bounded RECENT-window\n377\t        read on a large spine. Fewer than `n` if the spine is shorter. NOTE: a bounded window collapses\n378\t        a RAPID (recent) replay flood, but does NOT bound AGGREGATE replay bloat — a rotated pool of\n379\t        distinct bodies larger than the window each ages out and re-records. Only pair `tail()`-based\n380\t        dedup with a record-time freshness gate (or an independent bound); do not rely on it alone to\n381\t        close a bloat sink.\"\"\"\n382\t        if n <= 0 or not self._active.exists():\n383\t            return []\n384\t        with self._active.open(\"rb\") as f:\n385\t            f.seek(0, os.SEEK_END)\n386\t            pos = f.tell()\n387\t            buf = b\"\"\n388\t            while pos > 0 and buf.count(b\"\\n\") <= n:\n389\t                step = min(65536, pos)\n390\t                pos -= step\n391\t                f.seek(pos)\n392\t                buf = f.read(step) + buf\n393\t        recs: list[SpineRecord] = []\n394\t        for ln in [x for x in buf.split(b\"\\n\") if x.strip()][-n:]:\n395\t            try:\n396\t                recs.append(SpineRecord.from_dict(json.loads(ln)))\n397\t            except (ValueError, KeyError, TypeError):\n398\t                continue\n399\t        return recs\n400\t\n401\t    @property\n402\t    def next_seq(self) -> int:\n403\t        return (self._last.seq + 1) if self._last else 0\n404\t\n405\t    def count(self) -> int:\n406\t        return sum(1 for _ in self.iter_records())\n407\t\n408\t    # --- integrity ----------------------------------------------------------------\n409\t    def entries(self) -> list[ChainEntry]:\n410\t        return [\n411\t            ChainEntry(seq=r.seq, prev_hash=r.prev_hash, cert_digest=r.cert_digest, entry_hash=r.entry_hash)\n412\t            for r in self.iter_records()\n413\t        ]\n414\t\n415\t    def verify(self) -> tuple[bool, str]:\n416\t        \"\"\"Two-layer UNKEYED integrity: (1) BINDING — each record's payload still hashes to its\n417\t        stored cert_digest (catches silent payload edits); (2) CHAIN — the entries link cleanly\n418\t        (catches delete/reorder/entry tamper). This proves internal CONSISTENCY, not authenticity:\n419\t        a naive payload edit fails (1), and a mid-chain digest edit cascades an entry_hash/prev_hash\n420\t        break caught by (2) — BUT a writer who recomputes cert_digest+entry_hash for the tip (no\n421\t        successor to cascade into) or forward-cascades a fork produces a self-consistent chain that\n422\t        passes here. Resistance to a recompute-capable writer is the owner-SIGNED head's job\n423\t        (`checkpoint.verify_checkpoint`, Ed25519 + monotonic last_seq). Use this for corruption/\n424\t        naive-tamper detection; use the signed head for tamper-EVIDENCE.\"\"\"\n425\t        entries: list[ChainEntry] = []\n426\t        for r in self.iter_records():\n427\t            content = {\n428\t                \"scope\": r.scope, \"kind\": r.kind, \"source\": r.source, \"actor\": r.actor,\n429\t                \"payload\": r.payload, \"parent_id\": r.parent_id, \"supersedes_id\": r.supersedes_id,\n430\t            }\n431\t            if digest_payload(content) != r.cert_digest:\n432\t                return False, f\"binding break at seq {r.seq}: payload does not match cert_digest (record tampered)\"\n433\t            entries.append(ChainEntry(seq=r.seq, prev_hash=r.prev_hash, cert_digest=r.cert_digest, entry_hash=r.entry_hash))\n434\t        return verify_chain(entries)\n435\t\n436\t    def _read_last_entry(self) -> ChainEntry | None:\n437\t        # `_last_nonempty_line` skips a torn/garbage tail and returns the last VALID line (FIX 2), so a\n438\t        # crash mid-write can no longer block a restart. The returned line is guaranteed parseable.\n439\t        line = _last_nonempty_line(self._active) if self._active.exists() else None\n440\t        if not line:\n441\t            return None\n442\t        d = json.loads(line)\n443\t        return ChainEntry(seq=d[\"seq\"], prev_hash=d[\"prev_hash\"], cert_digest=d[\"cert_digest\"], entry_hash=d[\"entry_hash\"])\n444\t\n445\t    # --- seq -> byte-offset index (FIX 1) -----------------------------------------\n446\t    def _start_offset_for(self, since_seq: int) -> int:\n447\t        \"\"\"Byte offset to seek so a forward read yields exactly seq > since_seq. A full read\n448\t        (since_seq < 0) starts at 0 WITHOUT building the index — full scans stay a single byte-identical\n449\t        pass. Otherwise the index gives an O(1) seek to the line of seq (since_seq + 1).\"\"\"\n450\t        if since_seq < 0:\n451\t            return 0\n452\t        self._ensure_index()\n453\t        with self._index_lock:\n454\t            off = self._offsets.get(since_seq + 1)\n455\t            if off is not None:\n456\t                return off\n457\t            if since_seq + 1 > self._max_seq:\n458\t                return self._scan_pos              # nothing beyond the tip → the read yields nothing\n459\t        return 0                                    # below the min, or a skipped/corrupt gap → safe full scan\n460\t\n461\t    def _ensure_index(self) -> None:\n462\t        \"\"\"Build the index lazily (one unavoidable scan) and keep it current. Detects a file that GREW\n463\t        (our own or another PROCESS's appends — append-only ⇒ offsets never move, so we only EXTEND) and\n464\t        a file that SHRANK / was rewritten in place smaller (rebuild). Thread-safe under `_index_lock`.\"\"\"\n465\t        try:\n466\t            size = self._active.stat().st_size if self._active.exists() else 0\n467\t        except OSError:\n468\t            return\n469\t        with self._index_lock:\n470\t            if not self._index_built:\n471\t                self._offsets = {}\n472\t                self._max_seq = -1\n473\t                self._scan_pos = 0\n474\t                self._index_built = True\n475\t                self._scan_from(0, size)\n476\t            elif size > self._scan_pos:\n477\t                self._scan_from(self._scan_pos, size)      # extend forward over the newly-appended bytes\n478\t            elif size < self._scan_pos:\n479\t                self._offsets = {}                          # truncated/rewritten smaller → rebuild\n480\t                self._max_seq = -1\n481\t                self._scan_pos = 0\n482\t                self._scan_from(0, size)\n483\t\n484\t    def _scan_from(self, start: int, size: int) -> None:\n485\t        \"\"\"Index every COMPLETE (newline-terminated) record line in bytes [start, size). MUST hold\n486\t        `_index_lock`. A malformed complete line is left OUT of the index (so a mid-file gap still\n487\t        surfaces via verify()); a trailing partial line (no newline yet) is left for the next extend.\"\"\"\n488\t        if size <= start:\n489\t            return\n490\t        with self._active.open(\"rb\") as f:\n491\t            f.seek(start)\n492\t            chunk = f.read(size - start)\n493\t        consumed = 0\n494\t        while True:\n495\t            nl = chunk.find(b\"\\n\", consumed)\n496\t            if nl == -1:\n497\t                break                                       # trailing partial line — not complete yet\n498\t            raw = chunk[consumed:nl]\n499\t            line_off = start + consumed\n500\t            consumed = nl + 1\n501\t            if not raw.strip():\n502\t                continue\n503\t            try:\n504\t                d = json.loads(raw)\n505\t                if not all(k in d for k in _REQUIRED_KEYS):\n506\t                    raise KeyError\n507\t                seq = d[\"seq\"]\n508\t            except (ValueError, KeyError, TypeError):\n509\t                continue                                    # corrupt complete line — do not index it\n510\t            self._offsets[seq] = line_off\n511\t            if seq > self._max_seq:\n512\t                self._max_seq = seq\n513\t        self._scan_pos = start + consumed\n514\t"}]},"uuid":"5eec7132-09c3-4148-902e-43c0f8cd67d0","timestamp":"2026-07-19T15:53:11.337Z","sourceToolAssistantUUID":"15249b8c-089e-456e-bf72-cb16c9146f69","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-vscode","cwd":"/home/kali/Pictures/PENTEST-main","sessionId":"7758e121-f349-47d5-886b-6bb5a1d60e27","version":"2.1.214","gitBranch":"main","slug":"parsed-popping-lemur"}

{"parentUuid":"4e916259-6d66-4068-b55b-9333f34c60bc","isSidechain":true,"promptId":"58479281-f0fc-437a-b3c2-51154bb8cfd1","agentId":"a9761cd2dcb2a76fb","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01RBRTmqbM6qfrETxJtiyQQn","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t\"\"\"Durable, atomic file replacement — the one implementation the spine's crash-safe swaps share.\n2\t\n3\tExtracted verbatim from `checkpoint._atomic_write_text` (FIX 3) so the signed head, the manifest, and\n4\tany future single-file cutover all use ONE audited routine rather than drifting copies. The contract:\n5\ta reader observes either the whole old file or the whole new file (never a torn one), and the new\n6\tcontent survives a crash at any point — a crash mid-write leaves the PREVIOUS valid file intact.\n7\t\"\"\"\n8\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n9\t\n10\timport os\n11\timport tempfile\n12\tfrom pathlib import Path\n13\t\n14\t\n15\tdef fsync_dir(directory: Path | str) -> None:\n16\t    \"\"\"fsync a directory so a rename/create inside it is itself durable across a crash. A no-op-on-error\n17\t    on filesystems that don't support directory fsync (the rename still lands; only its durability window\n18\t    widens).\"\"\"\n19\t    try:\n20\t        dfd = os.open(str(directory), os.O_DIRECTORY)\n21\t        try:\n22\t            os.fsync(dfd)\n23\t        finally:\n24\t            os.close(dfd)\n25\t    except OSError:  # pragma: no cover — dir fsync unsupported on some filesystems\n26\t        pass\n27\t\n28\t\n29\tdef atomic_write_text(path: Path | str, data: str, *, prefix: str = \".tmp-\") -> None:\n30\t    \"\"\"Durably + atomically replace `path` with `data`: write a temp file in the SAME dir, fsync it,\n31\t    `os.replace()` over the target (atomic on POSIX), then fsync the directory so the rename survives a\n32\t    crash. A crash at any point leaves the previous valid file intact, never a partially-written one.\"\"\"\n33\t    path = Path(path)\n34\t    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n35\t    fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=str(path.parent), prefix=prefix, suffix=\".tmp\")\n36\t    try:\n37\t        with os.fdopen(fd, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as f:\n38\t            f.write(data)\n39\t            f.flush()\n40\t            os.fsync(f.fileno())\n41\t        os.replace(tmp, path)\n42\t    except BaseException:\n43\t        try:\n44\t            os.unlink(tmp)\n45\t        except OSError:\n46\t            pass\n47\t        raise\n48\t    fsync_dir(path.parent)\n49\t"}]},"uuid":"b50a3380-84c9-49eb-a648-9b57e86ce5ae","timestamp":"2026-07-19T15:53:11.447Z","sourceToolAssistantUUID":"4e916259-6d66-4068-b55b-9333f34c60bc","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-vscode","cwd":"/home/kali/Pictures/PENTEST-main","sessionId":"7758e121-f349-47d5-886b-6bb5a1d60e27","version":"2.1.214","gitBranch":"main","slug":"parsed-popping-lemur"}

{"parentUuid":"ae2d5c94-5be0-495d-a606-6c0240af86e4","isSidechain":true,"promptId":"58479281-f0fc-437a-b3c2-51154bb8cfd1","agentId":"a9761cd2dcb2a76fb","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01Wc7nKrwcs1gM42SzV5Y5HY","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t\"\"\"Daily signed checkpoint of the spine head (SIGIL §6.3.6, WARDEN anchor).\n2\t\n3\tGenerates + persists a solo-owner Ed25519 keypair once (1-of-1 trust root), then signs\n4\tthe chain head so the whole spine is anchored: rewriting history would require forging\n5\tthe owner signature, and a shrunk/back-dated head is caught by the monotonic last_seq.\n6\t\n7\tNote: for a personal, single-owner, local-first system the owner's signing key lives\n8\tlocally (0600) — a deliberate simplification of the framework's \"keys never on the\n9\truntime host\" rule, appropriate to this threat model (§1.3). A hardware co-signer can be\n10\tadded later by raising the trust-root threshold.\n11\t\"\"\"\n12\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n13\t\n14\timport os\n15\tfrom pathlib import Path\n16\t\n17\tfrom ..config import HEAD_PATH, KEYS_DIR, OWNER_KEY_ID, SCOPE\n18\tfrom ..reuse import (\n19\t    AuthorizerKey,\n20\t    SignedChainHead,\n21\t    TrustRoot,\n22\t    generate_keypair,\n23\t    sign_head,\n24\t    verify_head,\n25\t)\n26\tfrom .atomicio import atomic_write_text\n27\tfrom .store import SpineStore\n28\t\n29\t_PRIV = KEYS_DIR / \"owner.priv\"\n30\t_PUB = KEYS_DIR / \"owner.pub\"\n31\t\n32\t\n33\tdef _atomic_write_text(path: Path, data: str) -> None:\n34\t    \"\"\"Durably + atomically replace `path` with `data` (FIX 3) — a reader sees either the whole old or\n35\t    the whole new head, never a torn one, and a crash leaves the previous valid head intact. Delegates to\n36\t    the one shared `spine.atomicio.atomic_write_text` so the head, the manifest, and every cutover use the\n37\t    same audited routine (no drift).\"\"\"\n38\t    atomic_write_text(path, data, prefix=\".head-\")\n39\t\n40\t\n41\tdef _owner_keys() -> tuple[str, str]:\n42\t    if not _PRIV.exists():\n43\t        KEYS_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n44\t        kp = generate_keypair()\n45\t        _PRIV.write_text(kp.private_key_b64, encoding=\"utf-8\")\n46\t        os.chmod(_PRIV, 0o600)\n47\t        _PUB.write_text(kp.public_key_b64, encoding=\"utf-8\")\n48\t    return _PRIV.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\").strip(), _PUB.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\").strip()\n49\t\n50\t\n51\tdef trust_root() -> TrustRoot:\n52\t    _, pub = _owner_keys()\n53\t    return TrustRoot(threshold=1, authorizers=[\n54\t        AuthorizerKey(key_id=OWNER_KEY_ID, name=\"owner\", public_key_b64=pub)])\n55\t\n56\t\n57\tdef checkpoint(store: SpineStore | None = None) -> SignedChainHead:\n58\t    store = store or SpineStore()\n59\t    priv, _ = _owner_keys()\n60\t    head = sign_head(store.entries(), engagement_slug=SCOPE, signers=[(OWNER_KEY_ID, priv)])\n61\t    _atomic_write_text(HEAD_PATH, head.model_dump_json())   # FIX 3: never leave a torn head on a crash\n62\t    return head\n63\t\n64\t\n65\tdef classify_head(head: SignedChainHead, entries: list, tr: TrustRoot) -> tuple[bool, str]:\n66\t    \"\"\"Pure head/chain classification (no globals — testable in isolation). Distinguishes\n67\t    three cases honestly: a shrunk chain (truncation) or a mismatching prefix (history\n68\t    rewrite) are TAMPERING; a chain that merely grew past the anchor is benign — stale.\n69\t    \"\"\"\n70\t    n, signed_n = len(entries), head.entry_count\n71\t    if n < signed_n:\n72\t        return False, f\"TAMPERING: chain has {n} records but the signed head anchors {signed_n} (truncated/rolled back)\"\n73\t    # verify the head against exactly the prefix it signed; append-only ⇒ the prefix is byte-identical.\n74\t    ok, msg = verify_head(head, entries[:signed_n], tr)\n75\t    if not ok:\n76\t        return False, f\"TAMPERING: history rewritten at or below the signed head — {msg}\"\n77\t    if n > signed_n:\n78\t        return True, f\"anchors {signed_n} records; {n - signed_n} appended since — run `sigil sign` to re-anchor\"\n79\t    return True, f\"anchors all {signed_n} records (current)\"\n80\t\n81\t\n82\tdef verify_checkpoint(store: SpineStore | None = None) -> tuple[bool, str]:\n83\t    store = store or SpineStore()\n84\t    if not HEAD_PATH.exists():\n85\t        return False, \"no signed head — run `sigil sign` to anchor the spine\"\n86\t    head = SignedChainHead.model_validate_json(HEAD_PATH.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n87\t    return classify_head(head, store.entries(), trust_root())\n88\t"}]},"uuid":"0643c7f0-efd9-40f1-8b19-65f44ee94b4a","timestamp":"2026-07-19T15:53:11.735Z","sourceToolAssistantUUID":"ae2d5c94-5be0-495d-a606-6c0240af86e4","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-vscode","cwd":"/home/kali/Pictures/PENTEST-main","sessionId":"7758e121-f349-47d5-886b-6bb5a1d60e27","version":"2.1.214","gitBranch":"main","slug":"parsed-popping-lemur"}

{"parentUuid":"b820948e-8586-46dd-a492-d46ec7568c9a","isSidechain":true,"promptId":"58479281-f0fc-437a-b3c2-51154bb8cfd1","agentId":"a9761cd2dcb2a76fb","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01Kvevmv8cHysRPQLWtVN24G","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t\"\"\"Device-signed, replay-resistant request envelope (Phase 9 W1-A) — the bridge auth keystone.\n2\t\n3\tThe phone (a device the owner AUTHORIZED via `sigil.mesh.authorize_device`) signs EACH request to the\n4\tdesktop bridge with ITS OWN Ed25519 key over the canonical envelope core. There is NO wire bearer\n5\tsecret: authentication IS the signature, verified against the owner-minted authorized-device set. This\n6\tmirrors the approval-record pattern (`agents.approvals._approval_message` / `verify_approval`) — same\n7\tcanonical-JSON message, same fail-closed `verify_one`, same trust pinned to owner-minted device keys\n8\t(a rogue/revoked device cannot self-authorize; a tampered field breaks the signature).\n9\t\n10\tReplay resistance is a deterministic, spine-anchored monotonic-nonce highwater PER DEVICE, enforced\n11\tATOMICALLY for EFFECTFUL requests: the check-then-receipt runs under the spine lock (re-entrant), so\n12\tconcurrent replays of one captured envelope can't both pass. An effectful request must carry a nonce\n13\tstrictly greater than the highest nonce that device has ever been receipted for. Reads are authenticated\n14\tby signature alone (the transport verifies them without a receipt and bounds their replay with a\n15\ttimestamp window). The receipt is an append-only spine event, so the watermark is tamper-evident memory.\n16\t\n17\tThis module is PURE by construction — NO wallclock, NO RNG. The caller supplies `nonce` and `ts` so the\n18\tJS phone client and Python reproduce the exact signed bytes (the parity contract) and so freshness is a\n19\tdeterministic function of the spine. A wallclock timestamp-WINDOW check (is `ts` recent?) belongs to\n20\tthe server transport layer, not here. Offense-free.\"\"\"\n21\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n22\t\n23\tfrom typing import Set, Tuple, Union\n24\t\n25\tfrom ..reuse import canonical_json, sign, verify_one\n26\tfrom ..spine.store import SpineStore\n27\t\n28\t# The request vocabulary the bridge accepts — a fail-closed allow-list. `panic`/`relay` are effectful;\n29\t# the `read:*` family is side-effect-free. An action outside this set is refused even if validly signed.\n30\tACTIONS = frozenset({\"panic\", \"relay\", \"read:snapshot\", \"read:pending\", \"read:record\",\n31\t                     \"read:stream\", \"read:recall\"})\n32\t\n33\t# The spine signal marking a consumed request. Its records form the per-device nonce highwater.\n34\tRECEIPT_SIGNAL = \"mesh.request\"\n35\t\n36\t\n37\tdef envelope_message(core: dict) -> bytes:\n38\t    \"\"\"The exact bytes signed/verified — canonical JSON of the core. This is the JS<->Python parity\n39\t    contract: a future JS client MUST produce these identical bytes. Mirrors\n40\t    `agents.approvals._approval_message` (return bytes; encode only if `canonical_json` gave a str).\"\"\"\n41\t    m = canonical_json(core)\n42\t    return m if isinstance(m, bytes) else m.encode()\n43\t\n44\t\n45\tdef build_core(device_pubkey: str, action: str, args: dict, nonce, ts) -> dict:\n46\t    \"\"\"The signed core. `nonce`/`ts` are caller-supplied (this module never reads a clock or RNG).\"\"\"\n47\t    return {\"v\": 1, \"device\": device_pubkey, \"action\": action, \"args\": args, \"nonce\": nonce, \"ts\": ts}\n48\t\n49\t\n50\tdef sign_envelope(device_key, core: dict) -> dict:\n51\t    \"\"\"Phone/test side: attach a DEVICE signature over the canonical core, producing the wire payload.\"\"\"\n52\t    return {**core, \"sig\": sign(device_key.private_key_b64, envelope_message(core))}\n53\t\n54\t\n55\tdef verify_envelope(payload, authorized: Set[str]) -> Tuple[bool, Union[dict, str]]:\n56\t    \"\"\"Fail-closed authentication. Rebuild the core (payload minus `sig`); refuse if there is no sig /\n57\t    no device / the device is not in the owner-minted authorized set; then Ed25519-verify the signature\n58\t    over the canonical core; finally require the (now-authenticated) action to be in the `ACTIONS`\n59\t    allow-list. Mirrors `agents.approvals.verify_approval`. Returns (True, core) or (False, reason).\"\"\"\n60\t    p = payload.payload if hasattr(payload, \"payload\") else payload\n61\t    sig = p.get(\"sig\")\n62\t    device = p.get(\"device\")\n63\t    if not sig or not device or not isinstance(device, str):   # a non-str device would crash the `in authorized` set test\n64\t        return False, \"missing/invalid signature or device\"\n65\t    if device not in authorized:                       # trust pinned to owner-minted device keys\n66\t        return False, \"device is not authorized\"\n67\t    core = {k: v for k, v in p.items() if k != \"sig\"}\n68\t    try:                                               # verify_one RAISES on a malformed-length sig\n69\t        sig_ok = verify_one(device, envelope_message(core), sig)\n70\t    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 — any crypto/decode error is a fail-closed refusal, never a crash\n71\t        return False, \"signature invalid\"\n72\t    if not sig_ok:\n73\t        return False, \"signature invalid\"\n74\t    if core.get(\"action\") not in ACTIONS:              # allow-list the authenticated action (fail-closed)\n75\t        return False, f\"unknown action: {core.get('action')!r}\"\n76\t    return True, core\n77\t\n78\t\n79\tdef record_receipt(store: SpineStore, core: dict) -> int:\n80\t    \"\"\"Append the append-only consumption receipt. Carries only the routing fields — never `args`\n81\t    (which may hold a subject) and never the signature; the record is auto-tier (an A0 event).\"\"\"\n82\t    return store.append(kind=\"event\", source=\"mesh\", actor=\"DEVICE\",\n83\t                        payload={\"signal\": RECEIPT_SIGNAL, \"device\": core[\"device\"],\n84\t                                 \"action\": core[\"action\"], \"nonce\": core[\"nonce\"],\n85\t                                 \"ts\": core[\"ts\"], \"tier\": \"A0\", \"decision\": \"auto\"})\n86\t\n87\t\n88\tdef device_nonce_highwater(store: SpineStore, device_pubkey: str) -> int:\n89\t    \"\"\"The highest receipted nonce for this device (-1 if none, so a first nonce of 0 is valid).
